title: 👉 Pasos básicos de Marinera Norteña | Aprende 3 movimientos esenciales

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The teacher uses a clear, step-by-step approach, demonstrating each movement slowly before increasing the tempo. She provides specific instructions for both men and women, emphasizing posture and the characteristic hip movements of the dance.

lesson_structure.note: Introduction of the teacher and the dance style.
Hip and marching exercises to prepare for the steps.
Detailed breakdown of the first basic step: Cepillado.
Detailed breakdown of the second basic step: Taco Taco.
Detailed breakdown of the third basic step: Punta y Taco.

common_mistakes: not keeping the support leg straight during hip movements
safety: Keep the core engaged (barriguita metida) to support the back.

steps_taught.name: Cepillado Cruzado
steps_taught.description: The foot brushes the floor forward, crosses over, and returns to the starting position.

steps_taught.name: Cepillado de Frente
steps_taught.description: The foot brushes forward, the knee bends, and the foot brushes forward again.

steps_taught.name: Taco Taco
steps_taught.description: The heel strikes the floor twice in succession.

steps_taught.name: Punta y Taco
steps_taught.description: The toe strikes the floor followed by the heel.

what_works: Clear visual demonstrations from multiple angles.
Specific instructions for gender-based variations in posture and hand placement.
what_hinders: The fast pace of the music during full-tempo practice might be challenging for absolute beginners.

quotes.text: Empezamos en el caso de las mujeres a mover la cadera.
La pierna de soporte va completamente estirada.
La barriguita metida y levanto mi mentón.
Recuerden que la punta del pie tiene que rozar el piso.

evidence_segments.observation: Teacher demonstrates hip isolation exercises for women, emphasizing the support leg.
Teacher demonstrates marching exercises for men.

extraction.distinctive_method: The teacher uses a 'mirroring' technique where she performs the movements while facing the camera, but also provides side and back views to ensure the student understands the 3D nature of the steps.
